title: Elm: Old Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: Elms whose species nobody has confirmed. Madrid's green guide calls the elm on the Paseo de la Castellana the oldest street tree in the city.
intro: These elms carry only their genus, Ulmus, because nobody has yet confirmed which elm each one is. Any old elm counts, since Dutch elm disease has been killing them across Europe since the 1920s. Delft's three at Jaffa cemetery went in between 1890 and 1900, already in the ground when the disease was named, and were grown as weeping arbours. Madrid's guide calls the elm on the Paseo de la Castellana the city's oldest street tree, a title it inherited when the two older ones were lost. The other two came from readers. Near Hatley in Cambridgeshire, one walker found what they took for a deer's leg bone wedged in a crack of the bark and named the tree after it. In Melbourne's Curtain Square, two readers on the same day took a furrowed giant for the square's Moreton Bay fig. If you know your elms, tell us.
